title: Topic Selection Best Practices
content: When selecting a research topic, consider: 1) Impact - will this matter to the community? 2) Novelty - is there a clear gap? 3) Feasibility - can you execute this with available resources? 4) Scope - is it neither too broad nor too narrow?
checklist: Conduct preliminary literature scan for each
Assess personal expertise and interest alignment
Discuss with advisor or peers for feedback
pitfalls: Choosing a topic that is too broad to complete
Ignoring existing work in the area
Selecting based on trends alone without genuine interest

title: Hypothesis and Idea Development
content: A strong research idea should: 1) Address a clear problem or gap. 2) Have a testable hypothesis. 3) Offer a novel angle or contribution. 4) Be positioned relative to existing work.
checklist: Search for prior work addressing the same problem
pitfalls: Not checking if the idea already exists

title: Experimental Design and Methodology
content: A rigorous research plan includes: 1) Clear baselines for comparison. 2) Well-defined evaluation metrics. 3) Dataset selection with justification. 4) Ablation study plan. 5) Risk mitigation strategies.
checklist: Define primary and secondary evaluation metrics
Plan ablation studies to validate each component
Identify potential risks and failure modes

title: AI/ML Experimental Best Practices
content: For AI/ML research: 1) Use standard benchmarks when available. 2) Report mean and standard deviation across runs. 3) Include computational cost analysis. 4) Address reproducibility (seeds, hyperparameters). 5) Consider ethical implications.
checklist: Run experiments with multiple random seeds (≥3)

title: Paper Structure and Writing
content: A well-structured paper follows: Abstract → Introduction → Related Work → Method → Experiments → Results → Discussion → Conclusion. Each section has a clear purpose and logical flow.
checklist: Abstract summarizes the full paper in 150-250 words
Introduction motivates the problem and states contributions
Related work positions your approach vs. prior art
Results include tables, figures, and analysis
Conclusion summarizes contributions and future work
pitfalls: Abstract that doesn't match the paper content

title: Revision and Quality Checks
content: During revision: 1) Check all claims are supported by evidence. 2) Verify mathematical notation consistency. 3) Ensure all figures are referenced and clear. 4) Check citation completeness. 5) Read from a reviewer's perspective.
checklist: Every factual claim has a citation
All figures and tables are referenced in text
Limitations section is honest and complete
Related work is comprehensive and fair
pitfalls: Figures that don't match the text

title: Submission Readiness
content: Before submission: 1) Verify venue formatting requirements. 2) Check anonymization (for double-blind). 3) Prepare supplementary materials. 4) Write a compelling cover letter if needed. 5) Double-check all links and references.
checklist: All references are complete (no 'et al.' only entries)
Code/data links are prepared (anonymous if needed)
PDF renders correctly on different viewers
Author list and affiliations are correct
pitfalls: Formatting violations leading to desk rejection

title: AI/ML Novelty Assessment
content: To assess novelty in AI/ML: 1) Search arXiv for similar approaches. 2) Check top venue proceedings (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAAI, ACL). 3) Look for concurrent work. 4) Identify your unique angle. 5) Articulate what existing methods cannot do.
checklist: Search arXiv with multiple query formulations
Check proceedings of top 5 venues in your area
Search Google Scholar for related terms
Identify 3+ differences from closest prior work
Verify no concurrent work submitted recently
pitfalls: Novelty claim based on application domain only

title: AI/ML Results Presentation
content: Present AI/ML results effectively: 1) Main results table with all baselines. 2) Ablation study table. 3) Training curves or convergence plots. 4) Qualitative examples. 5) Error analysis. 6) Computational cost comparison.
checklist: Main results table with baselines and your method
Bold best results, underline second best
Ablation table showing each component's contribution
pitfalls: Results without error bars or confidence intervals

title: HCI User Study Design
content: For HCI research: 1) Define target user population. 2) Determine sample size (power analysis). 3) Choose between-subjects vs within-subjects design. 4) Plan IRB approval. 5) Design questionnaires (SUS, NASA-TLX, custom).
checklist: Conduct power analysis for sample size

title: Systems Research Evaluation
content: For systems research: 1) Define workload characteristics. 2) Choose representative benchmarks. 3) Measure latency, throughput, and resource utilization. 4) Test at multiple scales. 5) Compare against state-of-the-art systems.
checklist: Select standard benchmarks for your domain
pitfalls: Benchmarks not representative of real workloads

title: AI/ML Paper Review Checklist
content: Before submission, check your AI/ML paper against common reviewer concerns: reproducibility, fair comparison, ablation completeness, clarity of contribution, ethical considerations.
checklist: Fair comparison: same compute budget for all methods
Code: availability mentioned (even if after review)
